- When sentiment is negative (especially > -0.5) in recent days, model tends to overcorrect downward; adjust forecast upward slightly to avoid underestimating rebound.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >+3% from prior 5-day avg), model often overshoots and overpredicts continuation; reduce forecast peak by 5–10% to account for mean reversion.
- If sentiment is neutral or mildly positive (0.0–0.3), model frequently underestimates upward momentum; add 1–2% bias upward for next 3–5 days.
- Model consistently underestimates true price in early forecast window (e.g., day 1–5 of 30d) when sentiment is weak; apply +1–3% bias to first 5 days if sentiment < 0.1.
- When sentiment turns positive after a negative streak, model often lags; delay peak forecast by 1–2 days and raise it slightly to match sentiment shift.
- If model forecast is >+2% above recent 7-day average, reduce by 1–2% to avoid overconfidence bias, especially if sentiment is flat or negative.
- For 30d forecasts, model tends to overestimate volatility in early days; smooth out first 5–7 days by averaging with prior 5-day moving average.
